title: Forge 10: RNN with backprop through time, and a GRU cell

wrong.no_tanh_derivative.py: the (1 - h^2) factor of tanh is missing from backward, so every gradient is too large
wrong.truncated_bptt.py: the gradient is not sent back through Whh (dh_next = 0): each step only learns from its own loss
wrong.dwhh_uses_current_state.py: dWhh pairs the gradient with h_t instead of h_{t-1}
wrong.dwhh_overwritten.py: dWhh is assigned at each step instead of summed, so only the first step's contribution survives
wrong.dwxh_last_step_only.py: dWxh keeps only the last step's contribution instead of the sum over time
wrong.ignores_intermediate_gradients.py: per-step gradients dhs[:, t] are ignored except at the last step, so a loss on every step is wrong
wrong.accumulating_grads.py: gradients accumulate across backward calls instead of being reset
wrong.stateful_start.py: forward starts from the previous call's final state instead of zeros
wrong.init_whh_unscaled.py: Whh ~ Normal(0, 1) instead of Normal(0, 1/hidden): the spectral radius grows with width and the state saturates
wrong.db_not_summed_over_time.py: dbh keeps only the first-processed step instead of summing over time
wrong.db_first_example.py: dbh uses only the first example of the batch
wrong.gru_gate_swapped.py: h' = z*n + (1-z)*h: the update gate has the wrong direction
wrong.gru_reset_before_matmul.py: the reset gate multiplies h before the matmul (the other published variant), which is not the cell specified here
wrong.gru_no_highway_gradient.py: dh drops the direct z * dh' path, which is exactly what lets gradients survive long spans
wrong.gru_dz_sign.py: the update-gate gradient has the wrong sign
wrong.gru_gate_sigmoid_derivative_missing.py: the sigmoid derivative z(1-z) is missing from the update-gate gradient

hints: Forward is a loop over time (that part cannot be vectorised away), but each step is batch-wide matmuls. Keep a (N, T+1, H) array of states with hs[:, 0] = 0 so step t reads hs[:, t] and writes hs[:, t+1].
Backward walks time in reverse with a running dh_next. At step t the gradient on the state is dhs[:, t] + dh_next. Push it through tanh with (1 - h_t^2), then you have da.

The same Wxh, Whh and bh are used at every step, so their gradients are sums over time: dWxh += x_t.T @ da, dWhh += h_{t-1}.T @ da (the PREVIOUS state), dbh += da.sum(0). Then dx_t = da @ Wxh.T and dh_next = da @ Whh.T.

For the GRU, h' = (1 - z) * n + z * h. Work from the end: dn = dh' * (1 - z), dz = dh' * (h - n), and the direct path dh' * z. Through the tanh and sigmoids you get da for the three blocks; the candidate block's recurrent matmul is scaled by r, so its dh path gets r and r's gradient gets q = h @ Wh_n.
Debug with finite differences one parameter at a time. If only dWhh is off, check you used h_{t-1}; if only early inputs are off, check dh_next is being carried.
